This is a named-complex page, not an area page: Hyde Park is one townhome community by Zenterra Developments near 28 Avenue and 156 Street in Grandview Heights, South Surrey, and Hyde Park Corner is a separate, smaller townhome phase on the same street. Hyde Park has no board sub-area and no SnapStats row of its own. The page text read displays no live listing cards and no feed count, so current availability on the page is UNVERIFIED.

items.t: The complex ground: Hyde Park sits near 28 Avenue and 156 Street in Grandview Surrey, north of Morgan Crossing, with Grandview Corners shopping about 1 km away (site copy). The page gives no civic address number for the main complex; MLS listing data for the complex uses 2888 156 Street and 15677 28 Avenue addresses, and Hyde Park Corner is at 2828 156 Street.

Board geography: there is no Hyde Park board sub-area and no Hyde Park row in the SnapStats data at all. The complex sits on Grandview ground in the Fraser Valley board community "S Surrey White Rock", so the Grandview sub-area row is the board context for this page's ground — it is not a Hyde Park figure. Any Hyde Park-specific inventory, solds, sales ratio, median or days-on-market figure is UNVERIFIED.
Per-sub-area median prices are not published (community level only): UNVERIFIED at sub-area level.

Planning frame for the ground: the City's approved South Surrey land use plans for Grandview Heights include the North Grandview Heights NCP, which designates land uses for the neighbourhoods north of 28 Avenue from King George Boulevard to Highway 15.
Transit: UNVERIFIED — no TransLink route timetable document for a route serving Hyde Park was opened in the research pass, so no route, stop or frequency claim is made here.

blocks.text: Good to know about Hyde Park South Surrey

items.t: Two complexes share one street and one name — and different stratas. Hyde Park (156 townhomes per the developer brochure; strata plan EPS2381 per the page, UNCONFIRMED) and Hyde Park Corner (2828 156 Street, 2021) are separate stratas, so two listings on 156 Street can sit in different complexes with different fees and documents. The page gives the main complex no civic address at all — "near 28 Avenue and 156 Street" — while MLS data puts its units at 2888 156 Street and 15677 28 Avenue. Establish the strata plan from the listing's legal description before anything else.
The 156 count is the one figure the developer itself backs.

Grandview's attached pool is the community's second-largest. Grandview carried 146 Condos & Townhomes listings in September 2026, behind only White Rock (193) of 593 community-wide, at a 14% sales ratio that sits mid-set — Sunnyside Park's 32% was the community's highest published ratio that month. Hyde Park resales are a single-complex subset of that pool, not a board category.

Floor-plan type is the real comparison inside this complex. The page states the complex was built with tandem-garage, double-garage and main-floor primary bedroom layouts (site copy), so two Hyde Park listings can be very different homes at similar prices — compare plan to plan, not just price to price.

Surrey's tax deadline is not the usual one buyers expect. City of Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty if not paid by midnight July 2 and a further 5% penalty after September 2 — a completion straddling early July needs the tax position settled on the statement of adjustments.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Hyde Park

items.t: OCP — Surrey: Surrey's current Official Community Plan is Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026 — Bylaw 18020 is never cited as current. The ground's plan layer also includes the North Grandview Heights NCP for the neighbourhoods north of 28 Avenue from King George Boulevard to Highway 15.
Zoning — Surrey: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 governs this ground.

SSMUH — Surrey, as the City states it: up to 3 units on lots under 280 m², up to 4 units on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, under the SSMUH zones in Zoning Bylaw No. 12000. Eligibility is parcel-specific; no SSMUH claim is made for the Hyde Park strata lots themselves, whose form is fixed by their strata plans.

Strata block (the tenure that governs both counted complexes, and any bare-land strata lot): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

faq.q: Are Hyde Park and Hyde Park Corner the same complex?
faq.a: No — the live page states Hyde Park Corner is a separate 16-townhome phase at 2828 156 Street, completed in 2021, with its own strata plan, so check which strata a listing belongs to before comparing fees or documents

faq.q: What should I check before buying at Hyde Park?
faq.a: Which strata the unit belongs to, then the package the live page itself names: the Form B information certificate, the strata bylaws and rules, the last two years of minutes and the depreciation report — plus the floor plan, since the page states tandem-garage, double-garage and main-floor primary bedroom layouts all exist in the complex

faq.q: Can Jared show me homes in Hyde Park South Surrey?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out what my home in Hyde Park South Surrey is worth?
faq.a: Jared prepares a home evaluation from recent comparable sales and the condition of your home. Contact him on 604-928-1361 or through the form on this site to arrange one.

faq.q: Is Hyde Park a neighbourhood in South Surrey?
faq.a: No — Hyde Park is a named townhome complex in Grandview Surrey, near 28 Avenue and 156 Street. A Zenterra brochure lists it at 156 townhomes in the developer's project history, and there is no Hyde Park board sub-area or SnapStats row.

faq.q: What market numbers apply to Hyde Park?
faq.a: None of its own: SnapStats publishes no Hyde Park row. The board context for its ground is the Grandview sub-area (Detached 66 / 9 / 14%; Condos & Townhomes 146 / 20 / 14% in September 2026) and the S Surrey White Rock community figures (attached median $700,000, 99% sale-to-list, 33 DOM) — context only, not Hyde Park prices. Per-sub-area medians are not published.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Hyde Park townhome?
faq.a: Long-term rentals cannot be restricted: the Strata Property Act amendment of November 24, 2022 removed that power province-wide, while short-term rental bylaws can still apply.

faq.q: What is the Lancaster Club, and does it affect fees?
faq.a: What the amenity costs to run is a strata-budget question — read it in the Form B package, not from the page.

faq.q: What market numbers apply to Hyde Park?

faq.q: The presales page says Hyde Park was built in 2021 — is that right?
faq.a: That line is site copy on the presales page's completed-communities list, and 2021 is Hyde Park Corner's year. MLS listing data for the main complex's own addresses states 2016.
